The October digest is drafted, brand-compliant, and logged. Nothing was scheduled and no subject lines were scored, as the brief and your instructions required.

**What I did**

- Fetched brief-012 and confirmed the target is the Tessera Labs newsletter segment, which covers all products and uses the community-organiser persona.
- Ran the brief classifier, which agreed it is a nurture campaign with low urgency and no legal review needed. Its review list was empty.
- Wrote the digest around the three tutorials from the brief: first riverbed pipeline, inspecting checkpoints, and schema evolution with mooring. The call to action is "Pick a tutorial and try it this week."

**Compliance decisions**

- The first draft failed. The Labs disclaimer was paraphrased, and the check requires the exact house text. The call-to-action check also landed in the review list at 0.56 because the body had a second ask, inviting readers to reply or open a discussion.
- I decided to treat the flagged call to action as a real problem rather than noise. The voice rules require exactly one call to action, so I cut the secondary ask.
- The second draft uses the required disclaimer verbatim and adds "experimental, community-supported" wording. It passed all four checks with no review items.

**Where things stand**

The passing draft is draft-camp-2026-10-012-02 and the Notion log entry is log-0012. The draft carries three candidate subject lines for the newsletter team, who send the digest themselves in the 2026-10-31 window.

Brief brief-012 is this month's Tessera Labs digest, a nurture email, not a launch. Draft it for the Labs
newsletter segment, run the brand check, and log it. Do not schedule anything: the newsletter team
sends digests themselves, and no subject-line scoring is needed for the digest.

House rules for every campaign: nothing is scheduled until the draft has passed brand compliance;
the subject line is chosen by the scored ranking, not by taste; when a decision tool returns a
non-empty review_required list, say what you decided and why; finish by logging the campaign in
Notion with a one-paragraph summary of what you did and the decisions made.

{"campaign_id": "camp-2026-10-012", "subject_lines": ["Tessera Labs digest: three riverbed tutorials for October", "October at Tessera Labs: pipelines, checkpoints and schema evolution", "Three short riverbed tutorials to try this week"], "body_md": "# Tessera Labs digest, October 2026

Hello from the Labs team.

No release this month. Instead, we wrote three short tutorials for riverbed, our streaming project, so you can get hands-on at your own pace. Each one is self-contained and takes well under an hour.

## 1. Your first riverbed pipeline

Start from an empty project, define a source and a sink, and watch events flow end to end. If you have never run riverbed before, begin here.

## 2. Inspecting checkpoints

Learn where riverbed writes its checkpoints, how to read them, and how to use them to understand what a pipeline was doing when it stopped.

## 3. Schema evolution with mooring

Schemas change. This tutorial walks through using mooring to evolve a stream's schema without rewriting what you have already stored.

**Pick a tutorial and try it this week.** Reply to this email or open a discussion in the repo if you get stuck. We read every message.

Until next month,
The Tessera Labs team

---
